claims.statement: The repository has no test runner configured and no unit/integration test files; verification rests on `pnpm type-check`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format`/`pnpm format:check`, and `pnpm build`, with no `test` script in `package.json`, no `*.test.ts` or `*.spec.ts` files, no `__tests__/` directory, and no `vitest.config.*`/`jest.config.*` files.

The only GitHub Actions workflow is `.github/workflows/openwiki-update.yml`, which runs the OpenWiki docs generator on cron/manual dispatch and does not invoke type-check, lint, build, or any test runner; there is no `pull_request` or `push` CI gate that runs the verification scripts on every change.

AGENTS.md codifies two `grep` commands under *Testing Changes* that act as the project's only security-policy regression test: a match in `grep -r "logger\.(info|error|success|command)\(\`.*\$\{" .` or `grep -r "console\.(log|error|warn|info)\(\`.*\$\{" .` is a compliance failure against the static-string logging rule.

The highest-leverage unit-test target is `redactSensitiveInfo` in `lib/utils/logging.ts`: a pure, security-critical string function whose three regex passes (provider-specific API key patterns, JSON `teamId`/`projectId` fields, and the env-var catch-all suffix set) must preserve variable names and mask values to first-4 + stars + last-4, with the known gap that `POSTGRES_URL` is not in the regex set.

`validateEnvironmentVariables` in `lib/sandbox/config.ts` is a pure table-driven function whose unit tests should pin down the per-agent required key (claude/codex need `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY`, cursor needs `CURSOR_API_KEY`, gemini needs `GEMINI_API_KEY`, opencode accepts either `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`) plus the always-required `SANDBOX_VERCEL_TOKEN`/`SANDBOX_VERCEL_TEAM_ID`/`SANDBOX_VERCEL_PROJECT_ID` and a non-null GitHub token.

The AES-256-CBC round-trip in `lib/crypto.ts` and the JWE A256GCM round-trip in `lib/jwe/encrypt.ts`+`lib/jwe/decrypt.ts` are deterministic primitives whose tests should pin down the empty-string passthrough, the `'Invalid encrypted text format'` and `'Failed to decrypt: …'` failure modes, and the property that `decryptJWE` returns `undefined` (does not throw) for tampered/expired/wrong-secret ciphertext - which is what lets a bad session cookie degrade to "not signed in" instead of a 500.

`upsertUser` in `lib/db/users.ts` has three branches that must resolve to one canonical user - (1) reuse an existing primary row matched by `(provider, externalId)`, (2) reuse the user from the `accounts` table when a GitHub external ID is already linked (the Vercel-then-GitHub path), (3) insert a fresh `nanoid` row - which are the canonical regressions to pin with unit tests.

`checkRateLimit` in `lib/utils/rate-limit.ts` runs a UTC midnight-to-midnight window over `tasks` and `taskMessages`, excludes soft-deleted tasks via `isNull(tasks.deletedAt)`, clamps `remaining` to `Math.max(0, maxMessagesPerDay - count)`, and combines new tasks and user messages into one total; these four invariants are the date-window logic worth pinning with unit tests.

`createFallbackBranchName` in `lib/utils/branch-name-generator.ts` is a pure deterministic helper whose output starts with `agent/`, contains a sanitized timestamp with no colons or dots, and ends with the first 8 characters of `taskId`; this is the natural starter target in `lib/utils/branch-name-generator.ts` because the AI-driven `generateBranchName` requires mocking `generateText` from `ai`.

Three integration suites would catch regressions that no unit test can: (1) auth callback → user row → session with mocked OAuth and a Postgres fixture to exercise the Vercel-then-GitHub dedup path, (2) sandbox config → env gate → SDK call with `@vercel/sandbox` mocked to confirm `validateEnvironmentVariables` short-circuits before `Sandbox.create`, and (3) a migration round-trip via `pnpm db:generate` → `pnpm db:migrate` against a throwaway schema plus `scripts/migrate-production.ts` gated on `VERCEL_ENV`.
